We have mass spec m/z 224.120115... likely molecular ion M+? That mass corresponds to C16H16O? Let's calculate exact mass: C16H16O = 16*12.0000 + 16*1.007825 + 15.994915 = 192 + 16.1252 + 15.9949 = 224.1201. Yes matches. So formula C16H16O. DBE = C - H/2 + N/2 +1 = 16 - 8 +1 =9. So 9 degrees unsaturation. Likely aromatic rings (2 phenyl = 8 DBE) plus carbonyl (1). So structure likely phenyl-CO-CH2-CH2-phenyl? That is phenylacetophenone? Actually acetophenone is C8H8O? Wait acetophenone is C8H8O? No acetophenone C8H8O? Actually phenyl-CO-CH3 = C8H8O? That's 120. Here we have C16H16O, could be benzyl phenyl ketone (phenyl phenylacetyl?). The SMILES we guessed: Cc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)CCc2ccccc2. That is p-methyl phenyl? Actually Cc1ccc(cc1) is toluene ring (methyl phenyl). Then carbonyl attached to that ring, then CH2CH2 phenyl. That gives C16H16O. Let's see NMR: 2.23 (s, 3H) likely methyl attached to aromatic (toluene). 2.81 (t, 2H) and 2.98 (t, 2H) are CH2-CH2 adjacent to carbonyl and phenyl. Aromatic: 7.17 (ddd, 7H) and 7.90 (ddd, 2H). That's total 9 aromatic protons, consistent with two phenyl rings (5+5=10) but one methyl substituent reduces? Actually toluene ring has 4 aromatic protons (since methyl replaces one). The other phenyl ring is unsubstituted (5). Total aromatic =9. Good. So the NMR matches our structure: methyl on aromatic (singlet 3H at 2.23). Two CH2 triplets ~2.8-3.0. Aromatic pattern: 7.17 (7H) maybe overlapping of both rings? 7.90 (2H) maybe ortho protons of toluene ring? But plausible.

Thus SMILES likely "Cc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)CCc2ccccc2". Could also be "Cc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)CCc2ccccc2". Validate with tool. Use validate_smiles.
